chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Humeed ibn Ziyad narrated to us, reading from his book, saying: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Hadrami narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad narrated to us. And from Yunus ibn Ya'qub from Salim al-Makki, from Abu al-Tufayl, who said: 'Amir ibn Wathila said to me:
"The one whom you seek and expect is only going to emerge from Mecca. He will not emerge from Mecca until he sees what pleases him, even if he is obliged to eat the twigs of the trees."

key_terms.الْأَغْصَانَ: twigs/branches (symbolizing hardship or sustenance in difficult times)
key_terms.يَرَى الَّذِي يُحِبُّ: sees what pleases him (a condition for emergence)

ai.seo_question: What are the signs and conditions regarding the emergence of the Mahdi from Mecca according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the Meccan origin of the Mahdi’s emergence, a key eschatological marker in Shia tradition. The phrase 'seeing what pleases him' is interpreted by scholars as the moment when the Imam perceives the fulfillment of divine promises and the removal of oppression, while the 'eating of twigs' signifies enduring severe hardship and patience during the period of concealment or pre-emergence.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (25) Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Sa’eed narrated from Hameed bin Ziyad from al-Hasan bin Muhammad al-Hadhrami and also it was narrated by Younus bin Ya’qoob from Salim al-Mekki from Abut-Tufayl Aamir bin Wathila that Abu Ja’far bin Muhammad as-Sadiq (as) had said:

“The one, whom you want and expect, will rise (and set out) from Mecca. He will not rise until he sees what pleases him even if he is obliged to eat the leaves of the trees.” Is there another way clearer than the way, with which the infallible imams (as) have declared and explained the matter of the disappearance to their Shia? Will one doubt the disappearance and the reappearance of al-Qa’im (as) after all these clear traditions?
